integrity: The proof separately checks countable-coordinate support for reals, properness of countable-coordinate subextensions, real coding of hereditarily countable sets, both bounds for the HC generating cardinal, and the published equality V[id_G]=V[G].
scientific_limitations: The conclusion uses the hypotheses under which the ownership source identifies the forcing with the product random algebra on 2^{omega_1}.
The term random integer is internal to a nonstandard arithmetic structure; the result concerns the object's external hereditary size in the ambient set-theoretic extension.
The exact generating-cardinal statement is restricted to families of hereditarily countable parameters; unrestricted generators can be singletons, as the random integer itself shows.
title: Honzik's random integer is not hereditarily countable
